label.en: Partner's means limit for qualified adult increase tapered withdrawal

description.en: Weekly means limit (€100) for a qualified adult (the claimant's spouse/partner) above which their qualified-adult increase (QAI) starts to be tapered away; the value has been stable since 2006, with only one recorded change. It is used as the withdraw_start parameter of BenCalc across several contributory payments: poact_ie (State Pension (Contributory), func_comment 'QAI: retirement age'), pdi_ie (Invalidity Pension, 'QAI: retirement age (until 2013)'), bunct_ie (Jobseeker's Benefit, 'QAI (reduced rate)'), and the shared AMtesting_ie block, whose comment notes it also implemented tapered QAI for Illness Benefit, Disability Allowance and Jobseeker's Allowance in 2006-07. This operationalises the Country Report's statement that 'qualified adult increases are gradually withdrawn as [the qualified adult's] means increase' (poact.md, bunct.md): once the qualified adult's own weekly means exceed €100, BenCalc's linear withdrawal formula reduces the increase.

label.en: Old-age increase

description.en: This is the flat weekly 'Old-age increase' (currently €10/week, unchanged since at least 2006 per the value history) added to a range of Irish social-welfare pension-type payments when the claimant is aged 80 or over. Defined centrally in ConstDef_ie, it is used as the comp_perTU of a BenCalc component across six spine policies: bfalp_ie (One-Parent Family Payment), pdi_ie (Invalidity Pension), poact_ie (State Pension (Contributory), commented 'Old-age increase: PR'), poanc_ie (State Pension (Non-Contributory)), psuwdct_ie and psuwdnc_ie (Bereaved Partner's Pension). The country report confirms this over-80 increase as a special condition of both State Pension variants (poanc.md: 'Increases for living alone and being 80 or over are also payable'), and poact.md notes that the increase is doubled when the recipient is also getting a qualified-adult increase and that qualified adult is also 80 or over.

description.en: This is the weekly personal (single-person) rate of contributory old-age/survivor payments made at 'State Pension (Contributory) retirement age' (66 and over). Defined centrally in ConstDef_ie and reused across the contributory-pension family, it is the 'PR' input to poact_ie's ArithOp calculation of the State Pension (Contributory) personal rate, a 'PR' comp_perTU component of pdi_ie's BenCalc for Invalidity Pension (whose recipients transfer to the State Pension (Contributory) at the full rate on reaching pension age, per pdi.md), and a comp_perTU component of psuwdct_ie's BenCalc for the Widow's/Widower's/Surviving Civil Partner's (Contributory) Pension, whose personal rate at or above retirement age matches the State Pension (Contributory) rate. It is also referenced in bfua_ie/BenCalc's Comp_Cond means test, matching the country report's statement that the Fuel Allowance means test is linked to the maximum rate of the State Pension (Contributory); its current raw value of €299.30/week (scaled by the constant $sw_weeks) matches the 2026 State Pension (Contributory) personal rate given in the benefits theme document.

description.en: The weekly Living Alone Increase, a flat-rate supplement added to the personal rate for claimants who live alone, usually alongside any qualified adult/child increases. Defined once centrally in ConstDef_ie, it is added via BenCalc's comp_perTU parameter in seven schemes: Disability Allowance (bdinc_ie), Incapacity Supplement (bhl_ie, not itself simulated), Invalidity Pension (pdi_ie), State Pension Contributory (poact_ie) and Non-Contributory (poanc_ie), and Bereaved Partner's Pension Contributory (psuwdct_ie) and Non-Contributory (psuwdnc_ie). description.en: This is the full weekly personal (single-person) rate of Basic Supplementary Welfare Allowance (bsa00_ie), Ireland's means-tested income support of last resort for people whose means are insufficient to meet their needs. It is used in bsa00_ie/BenCalc as the comp_perTU 'Amount' parameter, i.e. the base per-tax-unit amount to which increases for a qualified adult and qualified children are added before means are deducted, per the Country Report's description that 'the amount payable is the maximum rate applicable ... less means.' The benefits description document gives a personal rate of €242/week in 2025 rising to €252/week in 2026 (matching the constant's raw value of 252 per week). The modeller's comment notes that before the 2023 system this rate was pegged to the general working-age means-tested personal rate ($BenMTwa_PR, shared with Jobseeker's Allowance) but has since been set as its own separate constant, reflecting a policy divergence between the SWA and Jobseeker's Allowance personal rates.

Defined centrally in ConstDef_ie, it is used directly as the personal-rate component (comp_perTU) of the State Pension (Non-Contributory) in poanc_ie/BenCalc, and in bfalp_ie/BenCalc as the personal rate paid to One-Parent Family Payment claimants who have reached retirement age (per the model's own comment, from September 2006 such claimants receive the State Pension Non-Contributory instead of the working-age OPFP rate). The value matches the 2026 State Pension (Non-Contributory) personal rate of €288/week quoted in benefits.md (up from €278 in 2025); poanc.md confirms eligibility from age 66 subject to a means test and the habitual residence condition.

description.en: This constant is the reduced weekly 'qualified adult increase' (QAI) rate paid for a claimant's adult dependant under the working-age means-tested schemes, applicable to younger claimants who receive the reduced (youth) rate rather than the full personal rate. It is used in both bsa00_ie/BenCalc (comp_perTU, 'Amount') and bunnc_ie/BenCalc (comp_perTU, 'QAI: amount'), i.e. it feeds into the benefit-amount calculation for both Basic Supplementary Welfare Allowance and Jobseeker's Allowance. Per the benefits description document, claimants under the reduced-rate age threshold (under 25 for Jobseeker's Allowance per bunnc.md, under 26 for SWA per bsa00.md, unless they have qualified children or came from care/Disability Allowance) receive a reduced personal rate and an equal reduced qualified-adult increase of €163.70/week in 2026 (matching the constant's raw value), up from a corresponding reduced rate in earlier years. label.en: Official pension age

description.en: Official State Pension age used throughout the Irish spine; the model has held it at 66 since 2006. It is defined once, centrally, in the shared constants policy ConstDef_ie, and then referenced by 16 different policies (26 usage sites) wherever a rule needs to test whether someone is above or below pension age. Examples include the personal-rate/eligibility conditions of One-Parent Family Payment (bfalp_ie), Jobseeker's Transitional Payment (bfalpt_ie), Jobseeker's Allowance (bunnc_ie), Jobseeker's Benefit (bunct_ie, whose Country Report ties eligibility to 'pensionable age of 66'), and Basic Supplementary Welfare Allowance (bsa00_ie), as well as the point at which Invalidity Pension (pdi_ie) stops and recipients automatically transfer to State Pension (Contributory). It is also the age threshold behind the 'must be 66 or over' eligibility rules for State Pension (Contributory) and State Pension (Non-Contributory) (poanc_ie, the benefit this batch documents), and the 'must be under 66' cut-off for the Widow's/Widower's/Surviving Civil Partner's (Non-Contributory) Pension.

label.en: Qualifying period: min no of months in work

description.en: The minimum number of months a claimant must have worked within the qualifying period to satisfy the social-insurance contribution condition for Jobseeker's Benefit (bunct_ie) and its Pay-Related successor (bunct_prb_ie); set to 9 months since 2006. It is applied directly as bunct_ie's eligibility condition (Elig/elig_cond) and sizes the eligible-months component in bunct_ie's and bunct_prb_ie's benefit calculators (BenCalc/comp_perElig). Because the detailed PRSI contribution-week history required by the real rules (e.g. 104 weeks paid contributions plus 39 weeks in the second-last tax year, per the Country Report) is not available in the underlying survey data, EUROMOD instead imputes months worked from reported employment months, setting it to at least this minimum for observed benefit recipients so they pass the eligibility test. Defined once in the shared ConstDef_ie policy and reused by other unemployment-contingent benefits across the spine.

description.en: The 50% rate applied to the second earnings band of the income-disregard schedule used when means-testing weekly earnings in Disability Allowance (bdinc_ie), One-Parent Family Payment (bfalp_ie) and Jobseeker's Transitional Payment (bfalpt_ie). It is passed as the band_rate parameter of each scheme's SchedCalc, for the band immediately above the initial disregard threshold ($ben_dis_thres). Per the Country Report, once the initial disregard is used up, 'half of subsequent earnings' (bdinc, bfalp) or '50% of the balance' (bfalpt) is disregarded, i.e. only half of further earnings in that band counts as assessable means.

It is passed as band_uplim, the upper limit of the first (fully-disregarded) earnings band, in each scheme's SchedCalc income test; earnings above it fall into a second band where only 50% counts as means (see $ben_dis_rate). This matches the Country-Report text for poact.md ('increases for... being 80 or over are payable... doubled if the recipient is getting a qualified adult increase and the qualified adult is also 80 or over'), poanc.md ('Increases for living alone and being 80 or over are also payable') and psuwdct.md ('Increases for... living alone or being 80 or over are payable'); its role within pdi_ie is less clear from the sources, since the pdi Country-Report section describes Invalidity Pension recipients as transferring automatically to State Pension at pension age (i.e. before turning 80), so this shared component may rarely bind there under current rules.

description.en: A shared age threshold (in years) used across several Irish means-tested payments to distinguish the full-rate ('adult') personal rate and Qualified Adult Increase (QAI) from the reduced 'young person' rates, and to decide which partner in a couple is modelled as the claimant. In the Jobseeker's Allowance calculation (bunnc_ie/BenCalc, the 'PR' component), a claimant aged at or below $ben_qai_age who is not the parent of a dependent child receives the reduced personal rate instead of the standard rate ($BenMTwa_PR_amt vs $BenMTwa_PR_rate) - matching the Country Report rule that 'people under 25 get reduced rates, unless they have qualified children, were in the care of the Child and Family Agency ... or transitioned from Disability Allowance.' The same constant is reused in the Basic Supplementary Welfare Allowance calculation (bsa00_ie/BenCalc, the 'Amount' component) for both the equivalent personal-rate split and the Qualified Adult Increase, and (via HasMaxValInTu/IsParentOfDepChild conditions) to assume that the older or parenting partner makes the claim - matching bsa00's rule that 'people under 26 get reduced rates, unless they have qualified children ...'. Across the systems modelled its value has risen from not applicable in the earliest years to 19, then 24, and to the current 25 shown here; because the constant is shared, EUROMOD applies this single threshold to both benefits even though the Country Report currently states a slightly higher cut-off (26) for Supplementary Welfare Allowance.

description.en: $ben_wth_thres1 is a weekly EUR threshold, fixed at €7.60 since 2006-01-01, used as the Withdraw_Start parameter of the BenCalc function that computes the personal-rate entitlement (for claimants under the state pension age of 66) in the psuwdnc_ie policy — the Widow's, Widower's or Surviving Civil Partner's (Non-Contributory) Pension, now titled Bereaved Partner's Pension (Non-Contributory). It sets the level of assessed weekly means below which the personal rate is unaffected: only means above this amount trigger withdrawal of the pension via BenCalc's linear taper. Both the Country Report and the theme description confirm this in the income test: 'the first €7.60 per week of means ... does not affect the rate of pension', after which the pension is withdrawn one-to-one as means rise further.

description.en: $ben_wth_thres2 is a weekly EUR amount, currently €3 (it has taken 5 different values since first being set on 2006-01-01), used as the Threshold parameter of the same BenCalc component in psuwdnc_ie that pays the personal rate of the Widow's/Widower's/Surviving Civil Partner's (Bereaved Partner's) Non-Contributory Pension to claimants under 66. In BenCalc, the Threshold parameter replaces the computed result with zero whenever it falls below this level, so it acts as a minimum-payment floor applied after the means-based withdrawal (governed by $ben_wth_thres1 and the one-to-one taper): an entitlement that has been tapered down to less than this weekly amount is paid as nil rather than as a token sum. The Country Report and theme description confirm the pension is a single personal-rate payment withdrawn one-to-one as means increase, but neither source explicitly discusses this minimum-payment cut-off, so its administrative rationale is inferred from the BenCalc parameter semantics rather than stated directly in the sources.

description.en: This constant is the weekly gross-earnings exemption threshold for Ireland's Health Levy (Health Contribution), the social-insurance-type charge modelled as the tschl_ie policy; per the IE country report's policy list, tschl_ie is labelled 'SIC: Health Levy (until 2010)'. In the model it feeds the Elig_Cond parameter of the Elig function in tschl_ie (func_comment "Eligibility"), which sets the liability indicator (sel_s) to 1 only for individuals whose weekly earnings reach this amount, so anyone earning below $tschl_lowlim per week is exempt from the levy. The Health Levy was charged alongside PRSI and, together with the Income Levy, was abolished and folded into the Universal Social Charge (USC) from 2011. The constant carries four distinct historical values from 2006 while the levy was active, but is recorded as n/a in the current EUROMOD system now that the policy is switched off; no concrete threshold figure is available from the sources reviewed.

Under BenCalc's linear-withdrawal formula (tapered = result − max(means − start, 0) × rate), each euro of the qualified adult's means above the applicable start point reduces the increase by €0.63, consistent with the pdi.md Country-Report statement that qualified adult increases are 'gradually withdrawn as the qualified adult's means increase'. The rate has been revised five times since 2006; neither the Ireland benefits summary nor the pdi Country-Report section states this fine-grained taper rate directly, so the specific figure's role is inferred from the constant's name/label, its BenCalc parameter (withdraw_rate) and the shared func_comment linking it to $pdi_qai_amt and $pdi_qai_thres.

Per BenCalc's documented Threshold behaviour, the function's result is replaced by zero once it falls below this value, so once means-testing has whittled the QAI down below €17.10/week the increase is paid as nil rather than as a small residual amount — mirroring how Irish DSP payment schedules cut off very small residual increases rather than tapering them down to a few cents. This figure is not spelled out in the Ireland benefits summary or the pdi Country-Report section (which describe only the general means-taper, not this specific cut-off), so the interpretation rests on the constant's name/label, its BenCalc parameter (Threshold) and the shared func_comment linking it to $pdi_qai_amt and $pdi_qai_rate.

description.en: The periodic per-child payment amount defined by policy bcc_ie, whose own internal comment in the model spine identifies it as Ireland's (former) 'Early Childcare Supplement ... (until 2010)' - a universal payment to families with young children that historically moved from a quarterly rate (e.g. €250 per quarter in the mid-2000s) to a reduced monthly rate before being phased out. It is consumed in bcc_ie's ArithOp function via the #_amount footnote parameter in the formula 'nDepChInTu * amount#1', so the total payment for a family equals this amount multiplied by the number of dependent children in the bcc_ie tax unit (as defined by the companion constant $bcc_depchild_age). The constant's current value is 'n/a', consistent with the scheme's discontinuation, and because the current (2025-2026) benefits theme document only documents live schemes and does not mention it, this description relies on the constant's usage and the defining policy's own historical comment rather than the provided theme/country-report sources.

description.en: Technical normalisation constant (value 1.1257, dimensionless) used only in policy tpr_ie, EUROMOD's implementation of Ireland's original, 2013-based Local Property Tax (LPT) on main residences. The spine divides the household's main-residence market-value variable 'amr' by it — (amr/$amr_2013) — before testing the result against the $tpr_valuation_band_1...19 thresholds in tpr_ie/Elig's Elig_Cond (gating which block of the calculation runs) and in tpr_ie/BenCalc's Comp_Cond (selecting the matching flat per-band charge, paid via Comp_perTU); the same normalised value is also tpr_ie/SchedCalc's Base for the two-tier 0.18%/0.25% rate charged on properties above the top band. Because LPT liability bands are fixed in nominal terms at the tax's 1 May 2013 valuation date while 'amr' itself is not, $amr_2013 rescales the property value to its 2013-equivalent level so each case lands in the legally correct band; it is a bookkeeping/index factor rather than a directly legislated rate or amount.

description.en: Technical normalisation constant (value 1.2184, dimensionless), the counterpart of $amr_2013 for a household's additional or other residential buildings besides the main residence (input variables aob01/aob02/aob03, gated by type-and-use flags such as aobtp0x/aobus0x) within the tpr_ie Local Property Tax (LPT) policy. Each (aob0x/$aob_2013) expression is compared with the $tpr_valuation_band_1...19 thresholds in tpr_ie/Elig's Elig_Cond and tpr_ie/BenCalc's Comp_Cond to place the building in a valuation band and trigger its flat charge via Comp_perTU, and is also used as tpr_ie/SchedCalc's Base for the 0.18%/0.25% two-tier rate applied above the top band. Like $amr_2013, it converts the building's reported value to its 1 May 2013 LPT valuation-date equivalent rather than representing a legislated figure itself.

description.en: $tpr_LPT_charge_1 is the fixed annual Local Property Tax (LPT) liability of €90 for valuation band 1 of the original, 2013-based LPT schedule modelled by policy tpr_ie (Ireland's property tax, introduced in 2013 to replace the flat Household Charge). In tpr_ie/BenCalc it is the Comp_perTU amount added when the paired Comp_Cond is true, i.e. when a property's 1 May 2013-equivalent market value — the main residence (amr/$amr_2013) or an additional/other building (aob01-aob03, each divided by $aob_2013) — is greater than €0 and up to $tpr_valuation_band_1 (€100,000). It equals the basic 0.18% rate ($tpr_LPT_rate_1) applied to the band's mid-point value, and per the Country Report (tprhm00) several of these band charges were carried unchanged into the post-2021-revaluation LPT schedule that superseded tpr_ie for later years.

description.en: $tpr_LPT_rate_1 (0.18%) is the first-tier rate in policy tpr_ie's SchedCalc, applied via Band_Rate to the portion of a high-value property's normalised 1 May 2013-equivalent market value (Base = amr/$amr_2013 for the main residence, or aob0x/$aob_2013 for an additional building) once that value exceeds the top standard LPT valuation band ($tpr_valuation_band_19 — the spine gates entry to this SchedCalc with Elig_Cond '(amr/$amr_2013)>$tpr_valuation_band_19'). A property's 1 May 2013-equivalent market value — the main residence (amr/$amr_2013) or an additional/other building (aob01-aob03, divided by $aob_2013) — falls into band 13 if it is greater than $tpr_valuation_band_12 (€650,000) and up to this threshold. description.en: Upper value threshold (€1,000,000) of the top standard Local Property Tax (LPT) valuation band (band 19) in the tpr_ie policy — the point at which the model switches from a flat per-band charge to a value-based formula for higher-value properties. It is used at three sites within tpr_ie: in BenCalc's Comp_Cond, to test whether a property's chargeable value falls in band 19 (triggering that band's flat charge, paired constant $tpr_LPT_charge_19); in Elig's Elig_Cond, where it most likely flags properties valued above this threshold as subject to the separate high-value calculation; and in SchedCalc's Band_UpLim, where it caps the first rate tier of a marginal formula (together with rate constants $tpr_LPT_rate_1=0.18% and $tpr_LPT_rate_2=0.25%) applied to properties above the top band. description.en: Weekly gross-income ceiling (currently €767.70) for the Fuel Allowance (bfua2_ie) means test, applicable to couples whose qualifying member is aged 66 up to (but under) 70 — the band between the lower ceiling for couples under 66 ($bfua2_means_couple_low, €698.70) and the higher ceiling for couples 70 and over ($bfua2_means_couple_high, €1,068). The value is consistent with the Country Report's description that the under-70 means test is linked to the State Pension (Contributory) rate plus roughly a €200 weekly margin: €767.70 equals the 2026 State Pension personal rate (€299.30) plus the qualified-adult increase paid for a partner aged 66+ (€268.40) plus €200. Despite defining this middle income band, the constant currently has zero usage sites in the spine (unused per the extraction), so unlike the couple_low and couple_high thresholds it is not read by bfua2_ie/BenCalc's Comp_Cond means-test condition.

It appears in that same condition alongside $BenCTret_PR_rate, $BenCTret_QAI_amt and $bfua_qai_amt, so it most likely acts as a margin added to the contributory pension rate(s) to build the weekly income ceiling(s) against which the claimant's income is tested. description.en: This constant sets the minimum weekly hours of employment required to qualify for the Working Family Payment (WFP, bwkmt_ie). It is used in bwkmt_ie/Elig as part of 'elig_cond' (comment: 'Eligibility (means test below)'), the condition that determines whether the family passes the work-hours test. description.en: This constant is the assumed take-up rate used to model non-claiming of the Working Family Payment (WFP, bwkmt_ie) among otherwise-eligible families. It is used in bwkmt_ie/BenCalc as the 'comp_cond' parameter (comment: 'Take-up adjustment'), where it drives a random allocation so that only a fraction of eligible units are treated as recipients. The Country Report explains that WFP has a relatively low take-up rate (Callan and Keane, 2008) and that the model adjusts for this by assuming 'only a certain proportion (33% based on earlier estimates) of those eligible actually claim it, using a random allocation,' matching this constant's fixed value of 0.33; this adjustment is built directly into the policy (distinct from the time-varying \$bwkmt_BTA_rate used by the separate BTA_ie non-take-up extension) and, per the Country Report, can be switched off directly within the policy itself.

description.en: Ad-valorem excise rate for COICOP category 02211 — Cigarettes (excise > ad valorem > 02211 Cigarettes). description.en: This constant is the maximum weekly rate of the income-assessed National Childcare Scheme (NCS) subsidy for children under 1 year old, equivalent to EUR 5.10 per hour over 45 hours of care. In the xcc_ie policy's BenCalc function it is used as the Comp_UpLim (upper limit) parameter, capping the per-eligible-child benefit component that feeds into the childcare-related benefit variable bccfc_s for this age band. Per the Ireland childcare-cost documentation, households with disposable income at or below the lower income threshold (bccfc_upthres1) receive this maximum rate, which then tapers down as income rises toward the upper threshold.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit maximum amount

description.en: This constant is the maximum weekly rate of the income-assessed NCS subsidy for children aged 1 to 3 years, equivalent to EUR 4.35 per hour over 45 hours of care. It is used in xcc_ie's BenCalc function as the Comp_UpLim parameter, capping the corresponding per-eligible-child component of the childcare-related benefit variable bccfc_s for this age band. Per the childcare-cost note, this is the maximum rate a low-income household can receive before the income-assessed subsidy tapers down toward the universal floor rate as household income rises.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit maximum amount

description.en: This constant is the maximum weekly rate of the income-assessed NCS subsidy for children aged 3 to 6 years, equivalent to EUR 3.95 per hour over 45 hours of care. It is used in xcc_ie's BenCalc function as the Comp_UpLim parameter, capping the corresponding per-eligible-child bccfc_s benefit component for this oldest age band. The Ireland childcare-cost documentation notes that the EUROMOD-HHoT implementation only simulates childcare costs for children aged 0-3, so this particular age-band ceiling is defined in the policy but not effectively exercised by the currently modelled population.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit maximum amount

description.en: This constant is the weekly floor (minimum) rate for the income-assessed NCS childcare subsidy, used in xcc_ie's BenCalc function as the Comp_LowLim parameter so that the per-eligible-child bccfc_s benefit component never falls below this amount as household income rises toward the upper income threshold. Conceptually this floor should equal the universal (non-means-tested) NCS subsidy rate, which the current childcare-cost note documents as EUR 96.30/week (EUR 2.14/hour x 45 hours) for 2025. The extracted value of EUR 63/week (EUR 1.40/hour x 45 hours) instead corresponds to the constant's effective date of January 2024, suggesting it reflects an earlier universal-rate vintage that predates the increase described in the current theme documentation; the exact correspondence is therefore not fully confirmed.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit minimum amount

description.en: This constant is the lower annual household disposable-income threshold for the income-assessed National Childcare Scheme subsidy: households with income at or below EUR 26,000/year qualify for the maximum age-specific subsidy rate (bccfc_maxamt1-3). It is referenced within the Comp_perElig formula of xcc_ie's BenCalc function, which computes the childcare-related benefit variable bccfc_s and linearly tapers the subsidy rate down as income rises from this threshold toward the upper threshold (bccfc_upthres2). This matches the low-income threshold documented in the Ireland childcare-cost note for the 2025 NCS parameters.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit income threshold

description.en: This constant is the reformed lower income threshold for the income-assessed NCS subsidy taper, intended to replace bccfc_upthres1 once a parametric change takes effect: the low-income threshold rises from EUR 26,000 to EUR 34,000 per year. Like its predecessor it is used within the Comp_perElig formula of xcc_ie's BenCalc function that computes the bccfc_s childcare benefit, setting the income level below which households receive the maximum age-specific subsidy rate. The Ireland childcare-cost documentation explicitly lists this change as parametric, effective September 2026.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit updated threshold

description.en: This constant is the upper annual household disposable-income threshold for the income-assessed NCS subsidy: above EUR 60,000/year income, households no longer qualify for the income-assessed rate and instead receive only the flat universal NCS subsidy. It is referenced in the Comp_perElig formula of xcc_ie's BenCalc function, marking the income level at which the linear taper of the bccfc_s benefit component reaches its floor (bccfc_minamt). This matches the high-income threshold documented in the Ireland childcare-cost note for the 2025 NCS parameters.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit income threshold

description.en: This constant is the reformed upper income threshold for the income-assessed NCS subsidy, intended to replace bccfc_upthres2 once a parametric change takes effect: the high-income threshold rises from EUR 60,000 to EUR 68,000 per year. It is used within the Comp_perElig formula of xcc_ie's BenCalc function computing bccfc_s, marking the income level above which only the universal (non-income-assessed) subsidy rate applies. The Ireland childcare-cost documentation explicitly lists this as a parametric change effective September 2026.

classification.reason: Childcare cost benefit updated threshold

description.en: This constant is the flat median weekly gross childcare fee (EUR 190) assumed for full-time centre-based childcare of children under 6 in Ireland, based on the national median fee for the 2022-23 school year, which is held constant under the Core Funding fee freeze. It is used in xcc_ie's BenCalc function (Comp_perElig, in the 'costs' component group) to compute the gross childcare cost variable xcc_s, which is annualised and deducted from adjusted disposable income (ils_dispycc). It represents the pre-subsidy cost baseline before the ECCE discount and NCS subsidies are applied.

classification.reason: Tax credit amount (likely child care credit)

description.en: This constant is the flat weekly value (EUR 64.50) of the Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) discount, corresponding to 15 hours of free childcare provision per week for eligible children aged 3 to 5 in Ireland. It is used in xcc_ie's BenCalc function (Comp_perElig, in the 'costs' component group) to compute the childcare discount variable xccdc_s, modelled as a negative cost that is added back to adjusted disposable income (ils_dispycc), partially offsetting the gross fee captured by xcc_amt. The discount is universal (not income-tested) and annualised over 52 weeks per OECD TaxBEN conventions.
